title: AI presenter
description: Putting a person on screen in an ad when there is no footage: the user's own clip first, or a generated portrait driven by a lipsync model. Covers when not to use a face at all, the lipsync input spec (portrait, audio, neutral mouth), framing and headroom for 9:16, one take length (four seconds), lip-sync tolerance in frames, matching voice to face, the uncanny tells and the edit patterns that hide them, the seek-safe build on each engine, and the line between a synthetic presenter and a fabricated customer. Load it alongside a UGC owner, never instead of one.
summary: A person on screen with no footage: the user's clip first, else a lipsynced portrait in takes of four seconds, framed for 9:16.

requires.why: Drives a generated portrait with a lipsync model. The only synthetic route.
Voice cloning and voice design, beyond the built-in generator.
One voice per project, chosen before any line is generated.
The narration the presenter is lipsynced to.
The portrait that gets driven by the lipsync model.
The user's own clip, which beats every synthetic route.
Trim each take and re-encode it with a keyframe on every frame before placing it.
The VO clip goes on the timeline at the take's start frame.
Framing and lip sync on plosives are checked on captured frames.

models.note: Drives a closed-mouth portrait; one take per line, four seconds or less.
Direct it flat. Over-performance is the usual failure.
Chest up, 3:4 or 4:5, wider than 9:16, mouth closed and neutral.
